pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis ( secondary to an Ovarian Teratoma ) THE SMOKING GUN: The presence of continuous oro-facial dyskinesias combined with the characteristic extreme delta brush pattern on EEG, prompting pelvic imaging that identified a mature ovarian teratoma. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: The patient's ectopic neural tissue within a mature ovarian teratoma expressed GluN1 subunits of N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors. This cross-sensitized the immune system, generating pathogenic autoantibodies (IgG against GluN1) that crossed the blood-brain barrier. These autoantibodies cause cross-linking and internalisation of post-synaptic NMDA receptors in the frontostriatal and hippocampal networks. The loss of NMDA receptor function leads to a predictable multi-stage clinical trajectory: early psychosis and memory deficits, progressing to catatonia, movement disorders (dyskinesias), hypoventilation, and severe autonomic instability. Treatment requires removal of the underlying teratoma alongside aggressive immunotherapy (IVIG, plasma exchange, and rituximab).
